source: Shem Tov Hebrew Matthew (Even Bochan, Ibn Shaprut c. 1385; critical text ed. G. Howard, base ms British Library Add. 26964)

verses.translation: Take heed{H8104} lest{H6435} you do{H6213} your righteousness{H6666} before{H6440} men{H120} so that they praise{H1984} you; for if you do, you will have no reward{H7939} from your Father{H1} who is in heaven{H8064}.

one_way_hebrew: צדקה (H6666) means both 'righteousness' and 'almsgiving' in Hebrew (Deut 24:13, where returning the poor man's pledge 'shall be righteousness unto thee'; Ps 112:9; Dan 4:24, where צדקה = giving to the poor). The Greek mss of Matt 6:1 split between δικαιοσύνην ('righteousness') and ἐλεημοσύνην ('alms') — two Greek words fighting over the one Hebrew word that holds both senses. The variant itself points back to a Hebrew original.
להלל (H1984) — the root of tehillah, praise; the hypocrite performs righteousness to harvest hallel that belongs to God.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (6:1): לפני] לעיני A ('before the eyes of'), על פני B.

verses.translation: Again{H5750} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to them: When you do{H6213} righteousness{H6666}, do not desire{H7521} to send a herald's cry{H3744} and trumpets{H2689} before you{H6440} like the hypocrites{H2611} — in the foreign tongue{H3937}, ipocrates — who do their righteousness{H6666} in the streets{H7339} and in the marketplaces{H7784} so that the sons{H1121} of man{H120} may see{H7200} them. Amen{H543}, I say{H559} to you, they have already{H3528} received{H6901} their reward{H7939}.

one_way_hebrew: The text glosses its own Hebrew word: החנפים בלעז איפוקראטיס — 'the chanefim, in the foreign tongue, ipocrates.' חנף (H2611) is Job's word for the godless dissembler (Job 8:13; 13:16); the Greek ὑποκριτής ('stage-actor') is here written into the Hebrew text as a visitor, exactly like evangeli at 24:14. A translator FROM Greek would have started from ὑποκριταί and never needed to gloss his own source-word.

כרוז (H3744) — the herald of Dan 3:4 (וכרוזא קרא); חצוצרות (H2689) — the silver trumpets of Num 10:2. The picture is a royal proclamation procession, fuller than the Greek's bare 'do not sound a trumpet.'
textual_notes: Shem Tov's section heading פרק כ״א (Perek 21) begins here.

Howard's apparatus (6:2): בלעז] לעז A; איפוקראטיס] איפוקריטיש A, איפוקריטאש BDG, איפוקרט EF; שיראו] שיכבדו ABCDEFG ('that men might honor them' — the Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew reads the same); אדם] האדם G.

verses.translation: But you{H859}, when you do{H6213} righteousness{H6666}, let your left hand{H8040} not know{H3045} what your right hand{H3225} is doing{H6213},

translation_notes: The ms shifts from plural ואתם ('and you all') to singular תעשה... שמאלך — the discourse narrows from the crowd to each man, a shift Hebrew makes naturally.

verses.translation: so that your gift{H4976} may be in secret{H5643}; and your Father{H1} who sees{H7200} the hidden things{H5641} will repay{H7999} you.

one_way_hebrew: הרואה הנסתרות — 'who sees the hidden things': Deut 29:28, הנסתרות לה׳ אלהינו ('the secret things belong to YHWH our God'). The Hebrew runs סתר/נסתרות on one root where Greek has κρυπτῷ... κρυπτῷ; and ישלם (H7999) is Boaz's blessing-verb, 'YHWH repay thy work' (Ruth 2:12).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (6:4): מתנך] מתנתך ABDEFG.

verses.translation: At that time{H6256} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to his disciples{H8527}: In the hour{H8160} when you pray{H6419}, do not raise{H7311} your voice{H6963}, and do not be like the gloomy{H6087} hypocrites{H2611} who love{H157} to pray{H6419} in the houses{H1004} of assembly{H3664} and in the corner{H4740} of courtyards{H2691}, praying with haughty words{H1364} so that the sons{H1121} of man{H120} may hear{H8085} and praise{H7623} them. Amen{H543}, I say{H559} to you, they have already{H3528} received{H6901} their reward{H7939}.

one_way_hebrew: בגבוהות — 'with haughty (words)': Hannah's prayer-warning, אל תרבו תדברו גבהה גבהה ('talk no more so exceeding proudly,' 1 Sam 2:3) — spoken by the woman whose silent prayer became the model of Jewish prayer. Greek Matthew has nothing here; it says only that they love to pray 'standing.'
מקצוע (H4740) — the Torah's corner-word (Exod 26:24); Greek has 'the corners of the wide streets' (γωνίαις τῶν πλατειῶν), the Hebrew 'the corner of courtyards.'
greek_deviations: 'Do not raise your voice' — absent from Greek Matthew; the Hebrew forbids loud prayer itself, not just its location.
העצבים — the hypocrites are 'the gloomy ones' already here at prayer; Greek attaches sad faces only to fasting (6:16, σκυθρωποί). The Hebrew uses one label for the same actors in both scenes.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's section heading פרק כ״ב (Perek 22) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (6:5): ישו] יהושע EF; העצבים] omit C; ובמקצוע] ובמקצועי ABD; שישמעו וישבחו] שיראו אותם ABEF, ושיראו אותו DG ('that men may see them'); אדם] האדם DG.

verses.translation: But you{H859}, when you pray{H6419}, come{H935} to your bed-chamber{H4904}, shut{H5462} your doors{H1817} behind you{H1157}, and pray{H6419} to your Father{H1} in secret{H5643}; and your Father who sees{H7200} in secret will repay{H7999} you.

one_way_hebrew: בא למשכבך וסגור דלתיך בעדך — Isa 26:20 in its own words: בא בחדריך וסגר דלתך בעדך ('enter into thy chambers, and shut thy doors about thee'). The verbs בא, סגר, and the distinctive בעדך are Isaiah's; Greek ταμεῖον ('storeroom') translates the same hiding-place. The same Isaiah text stands behind 24:26 ('behold, he is in the chambers').
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (6:6): למשכבך] למשכב B; דלתיך] דלתך B; בעדך] omit A; לאביך] + שבשמים G.

verses.translation: And you{H859}, when you pray{H6419}, do not multiply{H7235} words{H1697} as the heretics{H4327} do, who think{H2803} that by the multitude{H7230} of words{H1697} they will be heard{H8085}.

one_way_hebrew: אל תרבו דברים... ברוב דברים — Qohelet's own counsel on prayer: 'God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few... a fool's voice is known by multitude of words (ברב דברים)' (Eccl 5:1-2). The Hebrew stands in Qohelet's idiom; Greek βατταλογήσητε ('babble') is a hapax of obscure origin that translators have guessed at ever since.
greek_deviations: המינים — 'the minim,' the rabbinic term for heretics/sectarians — where Greek Matthew has οἱ ἐθνικοί ('the Gentiles'; some mss ὑποκριταί). The Hebrew aims the warning inside Israel, at the sectarian whose prayer is performance; the Greek redirects it at the nations.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (6:7): ישמעום] ישמיעון A.

verses.translation: Do you not see{H7200} that your Father{H1} who is in heaven{H8064} knows{H3045} your words{H1697} before{H6924} you ask{H7592} from him?

greek_deviations: The Hebrew reads 'Do you not SEE that your Father... knows your WORDS before you ask' — no 'be not like them,' and 'your words' (דבריכם) where Greek has 'what things ye have need of.' Mss ABEF read תדמו להם ('do not be like them'), assimilating to the Greek; the base text asks a question instead. The Father knows the words of the prayer before it is prayed — which is why they need not be multiplied (v. 7).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (6:8): תראו] תדמו להם ABEF, תראו להם DG; דבריכם] דברכם A; שתשאלו] ותשאלו EF.

verses.translation: And thus{H3651} you shall pray{H6419}: Our Father{H1}, may your name{H8034} be sanctified{H6942};

one_way_hebrew: יתקדש שמך — the petition of the Kaddish (יתגדל ויתקדש שמה רבא) and of Ezek 36:23 ('I will sanctify my great name'). The prayer opens inside the living Hebrew liturgy; Greek ἁγιασθήτω τὸ ὄνομά σου translates it.
greek_deviations: The Shem Tov prayer opens 'Our Father' — without 'who art in heaven.' Ms A adds שבשמים, assimilating to the Greek; the Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew also reads 'Our Father who is in heaven.' The base text is shorter than the Greek at every clause of the prayer (vv. 9-13).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (6:9): אבינו] + שבשמים A; יתקדש] התקדש EF; שמך] omit DG.

verses.translation: and may your kingdom{H4438} be blessed{H1288}; your will{H7522} shall be done{H6213} in the heavens{H8064} and in the earth{H776}.

greek_deviations: 'May your kingdom be BLESSED' (ויתברך מלכותך) — where Greek reads ἐλθέτω ('come'). The Hebrew echoes the Temple response ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד ('blessed be the name of the glory of his kingdom for ever'). The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew reads 'let your kingdom come' with the Greek; the Shem Tov form stands apart.
No 'as in heaven, so on earth' comparison: the will is done 'in the heavens and in the earth' as one clause.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (6:10): עשוי] עשויה D.

verses.translation: And give{H5414} our bread{H3899} continually{H8548}.

one_way_hebrew: תמידית — from תמיד (H8548), the Torah's word for the CONTINUAL offering and the continual bread of the Presence, לחם התמיד (Num 4:7). Greek ἐπιούσιον is a hapax so obscure that Origen said the evangelists coined it; the Hebrew לחם + תמיד is transparent Sanctuary vocabulary. A Greek translator facing לחם תמידית would have to coin exactly such a word; no back-translator from ἐπιούσιον would arrive at the Temple's תמיד.
greek_deviations: No 'this day' (σήμερον) and no 'daily' debate: the base text asks for the continual bread. Mss ABDEF rearrange to לחמנו תמידי(ת) תן היום לנו ('our continual bread give us today'), assimilating toward the Greek; G adds היום לנו. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew reads 'Give us bread every day, that it may support our lives.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (6:11): the whole verse in ABDEF reads לחמנו תמידית תן היום לנו (with spelling variations); ותתן] omit G; לחמנו] לחמינו C; תמידית] + היום לנו G.

verses.translation: And forgive us our sins{H2403} as we{H587} forgive those who sin{H2398} against us,

one_way_hebrew: מחל — the rabbinic and liturgical verb of pardon (the Amidah: סלח לנו... מחל לנו), with no biblical-Greek equivalent of its own; the prayer speaks the synagogue's Hebrew.
greek_deviations: 'Our SINS' (חטאתינו) — agreeing with Luke 11:4 ('forgive us our sins') against Greek Matthew's 'debts' (ὀφειλήματα).
translation_notes: מחל (machal) is post-biblical Hebrew and carries no Strong's number; it is the standard word for releasing an obligation or pardoning an offense.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (6:12): לנו¹] omit ABDEFG.

verses.translation: and do not bring us{H935} into the hands{H3027} of testing{H5254}, and keep us{H8104} from all{H3605} evil{H7451}. Amen{H543}.

one_way_hebrew: אל תביאנו לידי נסיון — the exact wording of the Talmud's daily morning prayer: ואל תביאני לידי נסיון ('and bring me not into the hands of testing,' b. Berakhot 60b). The Lord's Prayer clause exists word-for-word in the Jewish liturgy, including the idiom לידי ('into the hands of') that the Greek εἰς πειρασμόν cannot carry.

ושמרינו מכל רע — Ps 121:7, ה׳ ישמרך מכל רע ('YHWH shall keep thee from all evil'). The prayer closes by praying the psalm of keeping; Greek ἀπὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ ('from the evil one / from evil') translates it.
greek_deviations: No doxology: the Shem Tov text ends the prayer at ושמרינו מכל רע אמן, without 'for thine is the kingdom and the power and the glory' — the ending that also fluctuates in the Greek mss tradition.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (6:13): תביאנו] תביאינו B; ושמרינו] ושמרנו ADE.

verses.translation: If{H518} you forgive the sons{H1121} of man{H120} their iniquities{H5771}, your Father{H1} who is in heaven{H8064} will forgive your iniquities{H5771}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (6:14): תמחול] תמחלו ABDEFG; אביכם... עונותיכם] לכם G.
In the Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew this verse stands only in the margin, added in the same hand.

verses.translation: But if you do not forgive them, he will not forgive you your iniquities{H5771}.

translation_notes: The printed text carries a doubled לכם ('will not forgive to-you your iniquities to-you') — rough but intelligible; mss ABD smooth the first לכם to את, EF drop it.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (6:15): להם] omit G; לכם¹] את ABD, omit EF; the closing עונותיכם לכם omitted in G.

verses.translation: Again{H5750} he said{H559} to them: And when you fast{H6684}, do not be like the gloomy{H6087} hypocrites{H2611} who make themselves{H6106} appear{H7200} gloomy and change{H8138} their faces{H6440} to show{H7200} their fasting{H6685} to the sons{H1121} of man{H120}. Amen{H543}, I say{H559} to you, they have already{H3528} received{H6901} their reward{H7939}.

one_way_hebrew: ומשנים פניהם — 'change their faces': Job 14:20, משנה פניו ('thou changest his countenance'). And the Hebrew doubles one root — החנפים העצבים... מראים עצמם עצבים — the gloomy ones showing themselves gloomy: performance exposed by paronomasia the Greek cannot reproduce.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's section heading פרק כ״ג (Perek 23) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (6:16): אמר] omit A; וכאשר] כאשר EF; עצבים] עצובים B; צמותם] צומתם ABFG; קבלו] + את A.

verses.translation: But you{H859}, when you fast{H6685}, wash{H7364} your heads{H7218},

greek_deviations: No anointing: Greek reads 'anoint thine head, and wash thy face'; the Hebrew has only 'wash your heads.' The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew reads 'comb your head and wash your face' — each Hebrew text differs from the Greek differently.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (6:17): בצומכם] בצומיכם C.

verses.translation: so that you do not appear{H7200} to the sons{H1121} of man{H120} to be fasting{H6031}, but only to your Father{H1} who is in secret{H5643}; and your Father who is in secret will repay{H7999} you.

one_way_hebrew: מתענים — fasting called by the Torah's own name: וְעִנִּיתֶם אֶת־נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶם ('ye shall afflict your souls,' Lev 16:31 of Yom Kippur; Ezra 8:21 להתענות). Greek νηστεύοντες is the bare act; the Hebrew hithpael carries the Torah's category of self-affliction.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (6:18): אביך¹] לאביך ABDEFG; שהוא²] הוא A; בסתר²] + הוא F.

verses.translation: Again{H5750} he said{H559} to them: Do not keep heaping up{H6651} treasures{H214} in the earth{H776} for the rot{H7538} and the worm{H8438} to eat{H398}, or for thieves{H1590} to dig through{H2658} and steal{H1589}.

one_way_hebrew: לצבור (H6651) — Joseph 'heaped up' grain beyond measure (Gen 41:35,49) and Job's wicked man 'heapeth up silver' (Job 27:16): the hoarding verb of Scripture.

יחפרו (H2658) — thieves 'dig through' the mud-brick wall, Job's picture of the burglar (חתר/חפר, Job 24:16; cf. Ezek 8:8) — the same idiom behind 24:43. Greek διορύσσουσιν translates precisely this Hebrew burglary.
רקב (H7538) — the rot of Prov 14:30 and Hab 3:16; תולעה (H8438) — the worm that eats what is stored (Isa 51:8; Deut 28:39). Greek σὴς καὶ βρῶσις ('moth and eating') translates the pair.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's section heading פרק כ״ד (Perek 24) begins here.

verses.translation: Make{H6213} for yourselves treasures{H214} in the heavens{H8064}, in a place{H4725} where maggot{H7415} and worm{H8438} will not eat{H398} them, and in a place where thieves{H1590} will not dig through{H2658} and steal{H1589}.

one_way_hebrew: רמה ותולעה — maggot and worm, the fixed pair of the manna narrative (Exod 16:20,24: the hoarded manna bred worms; the Shabbat manna 'did not stink, neither was there any worm therein') and of Isa 14:11; Job 25:6. The treasure kept with God is described in the manna's own preservation terms — what is hoarded on earth breeds רמה, what is laid up with heaven does not.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (6:20): לכם] omit H.

verses.translation: In the place{H4725} where your treasure{H214} is — there{H8033}.

greek_deviations: The base ms ends the verse at 'there': it does not say 'there will your heart be also.' Every other Howard ms adds it (יהיה לבך BDEFG; יהא ליבך A), and the Greek reads 'for where your treasure is, there will your heart be also' — Howard prints the clause in parentheses. The base text leaves the sentence pointing: where the treasure is — there. The reader supplies where the man himself will be found.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (6:21): מקום] המקום A; שם] + יהיה לבך BDEFG, + יהא ליבך A.

verses.translation: And the lamp{H5216} of your body{H1480} is your eyes{H5869}: if your eyes{H5869} look{H5027} straight ahead{H5227}, your body will not{H1077} grow dark{H2821}.

one_way_hebrew: עיניך לנוכח יביטו — Prov 4:25 verbatim: עיניך לנכח יביטו ('let thine eyes look right on'), from Solomon's discourse on the two paths, which continues 'ponder the path of thy feet' — exactly the path-language this saying resumes in v. 23 ('all your ways'). Greek ἐὰν ᾖ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ἁπλοῦς ('if thine eye be single') paraphrases; the Hebrew quotes.
בל (H1077) — the Psalter's poetic negative (Ps 10:6; 16:8), natural to a Hebrew author, unreachable from the Greek.
greek_deviations: The base text states the promise negatively — 'your body will NOT grow dark' — where Greek states it positively ('thy whole body shall be full of light'). Mss ABCDEFG read כל גופך יזהיר ('your whole body will shine'), assimilating toward the Greek.
translation_notes: Howard's printed base text reads עיעיך at the first occurrence — an inner-Hebrew scribal slip for עיניך, which stands correctly in the next clause; the variants normalize it. The words array reproduces the printed reading.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (6:22): וניר] ונר AB; עיעיך] עינך A, ועיניך G, omit EF; בל... יחשוך] כל גופך יזהיר ABCDEFG.

verses.translation: And if the light{H216} that is in you grows dark{H2821}, all{H3605} your ways{H1870} will be dark{H2823}.

one_way_hebrew: 'All your WAYS will be dark' — the Hebrew ends on Proverbs' picture, דרך רשעים כאפלה ('the way of the wicked is as darkness; they know not at what they stumble,' Prov 4:19) — the very chapter quoted in v. 22 (Prov 4:25). Lamp, eye, and path belong to one Hebrew figure: 'thy word is a lamp unto my feet' (Ps 119:105); 'the commandment is a lamp, and the Torah is light' (Prov 6:23). Greek Matthew instead ends 'how great is that darkness!' — a measure of darkness, not a road walked in it.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (6:23): Beginning] + ואם עיניך כהו כל גופך יחשיך ABDEFG ('and if your eyes grow dim, your whole body will be dark' — supplying the negative half the Greek carries), + ואם לאו כל גופך יחשיך C; מחשיך] יחשיך ABCDEFG; כל... חשוכים] מחשכים יהיו כל דרכיך ABDEFG.

verses.translation: At that time{H6256} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to his disciples{H8527}: No man{H376} is able{H3201} to serve{H5647} two{H8147} masters{H113} without hating{H8130} the one{H259} and loving{H157} the other, or honoring{H3513} the one and despising{H959} the other; you cannot{H3201} serve{H5647} El{H410} and the world{H5769}.

one_way_hebrew: יכבד... יבזה — honor and despise: Malachi's own pairing about serving the Master: 'A son honoreth (יכבד) his father, and a servant his master: if then I be a father, where is mine honor?... O priests, that despise (בוזי) my name' (Mal 1:6). The Hebrew saying runs on Malachi's verbs of divine service; Greek ἀνθέξεται/καταφρονήσει translates them.
אל (H410) — the ms writes האל plainly here; the discourse's covenant name for God throughout the chapter (vv. 30, 31).
greek_deviations: 'You cannot serve El and THE WORLD (העולם)' — Greek reads μαμωνᾷ ('mammon'), an untranslated Semitic loanword. The Hebrew text names the rival master outright: the world. The saying then governs everything that follows (vv. 25-34): food, clothing, and the day of tomorrow are the world's service.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's section heading פרק כ״ה (Perek 25) begins here.
The ms abbreviates: והא׳ = והאחד ('and the other').
The circulating transcription reads והעלום; the scan of Howard's text reads והעולם — corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (6:24): לעבוד²] + את A; ולאחד] או לאחד D; יכבד] + לא B; האל] באל G.

verses.translation: Therefore{H3651} I say{H559} to you: do not be anxious{H1672} for the food{H3978} for your souls{H5315} nor for the clothing{H4403} for your body{H1480}, for the soul{H5315} is more precious{H3368} than the food{H4202} and the body than the clothing{H4403}.

one_way_hebrew: תדאגו (H1672, da'ag) — Jeremiah's word for the anxiety the trusting tree never feels: planted by waters, 'in the year of drought it is not anxious (לא ידאג)' (Jer 17:8) — the same trust-picture this discourse paints with birds and grass. The root recurs through vv. 25-34 as the discourse's spine; Greek μεριμνάω renders it each time without the prophetic anchor.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (6:25): לכן] באמת EF; שלא] לא A; במלבוש] בלבוש A; לגופכם] omit B, לגופותיכם EF; מהמלבוש] מהלבוש A.

verses.translation: Look{H7920} at the birds{H5775} of the heavens{H8064}, which do not sow{H2232} nor reap{H7114} nor gather{H622} stores{H214}; and your Father{H1} the Most High{H5945} sustains{H3557} you. Are you{H859} not more precious{H3368} than they?

one_way_hebrew: מכלכל (H3557) — the providence verb of Scripture and synagogue: Joseph sustained his father's house (Gen 45:11; 47:12), the ravens sustained Elijah (1 Kgs 17:4 — birds and sustenance in one verse), and the Amidah blesses מכלכל חיים בחסד ('who sustains the living in kindness'). The Hebrew word prays; Greek τρέφει ('feeds') reports.
העליון (H5945) — 'the Most High,' Melchizedek's title for God (Gen 14:19), where Greek has 'your heavenly Father.'
greek_deviations: The base text reads 'your Father the Most High sustains YOU (אתכם)' — the argument runs directly: the birds lay up no stores, yet you, worth more than they, are already being sustained. Mss ABDEFG read אותם ('them'), as in the Greek; Howard's English follows the variant with '(them).'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (6:26): אתכם] אותם ABDEFG; אוצרות] לאוצרות ABDEF, באוצרות G.

verses.translation: Who{H4310} among you of the anxious{H1672} is able{H3201} to add{H3254} one{H259} cubit{H520} to his stature{H6967}?

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (6:27): בקומתו] על קומתו EF.

verses.translation: If so, why are you anxious{H1672} about clothing{H3830}? Look{H7200} at the rose{H2261} of Sharon{H8289} — in the foreign tongue{H3937}, gilyon — which sprouts [?].

one_way_hebrew: חבצלת השרון — 'the rose of Sharon,' the Song's own flower (Song 2:1, אני חבצלת השרון), where Greek has the generic 'lilies of the field' (κρίνα τοῦ ἀγροῦ). And v. 29 sets against it the Song's own king, Solomon — flower and king from the same book, a pairing only the Hebrew preserves.

The loanword gloss runs Hebrew-to-foreign again: חבצלת glossed גיל״יון (cf. ms A ליריו — Spanish lirio, 'lily'), like ipocrates (v. 2) and evangeli (24:14): the Hebrew word is native, the Romance word the visitor.
translation_notes: החומש is obscure; the reading may be a corruption of הצומח ('which sprouts'), and the translation renders that sense, flagged [?]. Mss ABDFG replace it with בהגדלה אינה טוה ואורגת ('as it grows it neither spins nor weaves' — matching the Greek 'they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin'), and Howard's English follows the variant in parentheses.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (6:28): גיליון] ליריו A, גיליין BC, גילין DG, omit EF; החומש] בהגדלה אינה טוה ואורגת ABDFG.

verses.translation: And I say{H559} to you that King{H4428} Shelomo{H8010} in all{H3605} his glory{H3519} was not clothed{H3847} like it{H3644}.

translation_notes: כמוהו — 'like IT,' singular: like the one rose of Sharon (v. 28). Greek reads 'like one of these' (plural lilies); the Hebrew comparison is one king against one flower.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (6:29): ואני] ואיני B; כמוהו] כמוה ADEFG.

verses.translation: And if the straw{H8401} that remains{H7604} in the standing grain{H7054} — in the foreign tongue{H3937}, penon — which today{H3117} is fresh{H3892} and tomorrow{H4279} dry{H3002} and they put{H7760} it into the oven{H8574} — if El{H410} clothes{H3847} it, how much more us, who are of little{H6996} faith{H548}?

one_way_hebrew: מקטני אמנה — 'of the little of faith': the exact rabbinic idiom, attached in the Talmud to this exact subject: 'Whoever has bread in his basket and says, What shall I eat tomorrow? — he is of the little of faith (מקטני אמנה)' (b. Sotah 48b). Verses 30-34 (bread, tomorrow, anxiety) sit inside that saying. Greek ὀλιγόπιστοι is a compound calque of the Hebrew phrase; the Hebrew is the native idiom in its native argument.

קמה (H7054) — the standing grain of Deut 16:9; 23:26; תנור (H8574) — the baking-oven of Lev 26:26. Greek has 'grass of the field... cast into the oven (κλίβανον)'; the Hebrew scene is the harvest field, straw left among the standing grain.
greek_deviations: The base text reads 'how much more US (אנחנו), of little faith' — the speaker numbers himself with the hearers in the rebuke; mss ABDEFG read אתם קטני אמנה ('you of little faith'), assimilating to the Greek's ὀλιγόπιστοι address.
translation_notes: The loanword פי״נן (Howard transliterates 'penon') is a Romance word for hay (cf. Italian fieno, Old French fein), glossing תבן — again the Hebrew word glossed for readers who knew the vernacular.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (6:30): בקמות] במוץ EF ('in the chaff'); לעז] בלעז B; לחה] ליחה A; ומחר] ולמחר A; ומשימים] ומשימין B; אנחנו] אתם ABDEFG; מקטני] קטני ABDEFG.

verses.translation: And if El{H410} so thinks{H2803} of you, do not be anxious{H1672} to say{H559}: What shall we eat{H398} and what shall we drink{H8354}?

one_way_hebrew: שהאל יחשוב מכם — 'El thinks of you': the psalmist's confidence, ואדני יחשב לי ('I am poor and needy, yet the Lord thinketh upon me,' Ps 40:18). The clause is absent from the Greek ('therefore be not anxious, saying...'); the Hebrew grounds the command in God's mindfulness before forbidding man's anxiety.
greek_deviations: The verse opens with a reason the Greek lacks: 'if El so thinks of you.' The Greek moves straight to the prohibition.

verses.translation: For all{H3605} these{H428} the bodies{H1480} seek{H1245}; and your Father{H1} knows{H3045} that you{H859} need{H6878} all these.

one_way_hebrew: הגופים — 'the BODIES seek all these' — where Greek Matthew reads τὰ ἔθνη ('the GENTILES seek all these'). In Hebrew script the two readings differ by one letter: הגופים (bodies) / הגוים (nations). A Greek translator reading הגוים where his source had הגופים yields the Greek exactly; no path runs the other way, for a Hebrew translator of ἔθνη writes הגוים, not הגופים. And 'the bodies' is what the discourse requires — the body and its food and clothing have been the subject since v. 25. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew reads 'the peoples,' standing with the Greek and showing both readings alive in the Hebrew tradition.

verses.translation: Seek{H1245} first{H6924} the kingdom{H4438} of Elohim{H430} and his righteousness{H6666}, and all{H3605} these{H428} things{H1697} will be given{H5414} to you.

one_way_hebrew: צדקתו closes the loop the chapter opened: the chapter began with man's צדקה done before men (v. 1) and ends by seeking HIS righteousness first — one Hebrew word binds the frame; the Greek splits it across δικαιοσύνη and the alms-variants of v. 1.
textual_notes: First occurrence in this chapter of אלקים — the ms uses the reverent ק-spelling for אלהים.
Howard's apparatus (6:33): אלקים] אלהים A, אלים G.

verses.translation: Do not be anxious{H1672} for the day{H3117} of tomorrow{H4279}, for the day of tomorrow will be anxious{H1672} for itself; sufficient{H1767} for the day{H3117} is its own trouble{H6869}.

one_way_hebrew: יום מחר — Proverbs' phrase: אל תתהלל ביום מחר ('boast not thyself of tomorrow, for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth,' Prov 27:1). And the whole close answers b. Sotah 48b's 'What shall I eat tomorrow?' (v. 30 note): the man of little faith interrogates tomorrow; the disciple leaves tomorrow its own anxiety.

The chapter's spine-root דאג (H1672) sounds a final double beat — תדאגו... ידאגו — anxiety handed back to the day itself; Greek uses μεριμνάω/μεριμνήσει without the Hebrew's closing wordplay on the same root six times in ten verses.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (6:34): Beginning] + לכן ABDEFG; ידאגו] ידאג ADEF, דואג B.

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 6 in the Shem Tov Hebrew carries a Lord's Prayer shorter than the Greek at every clause, and a discourse woven on Hebrew roots the Greek cannot show. (1) The prayer (vv. 9-13): 'Our Father' without 'in heaven' (ms A adds it); 'may your kingdom be BLESSED' (ויתברך) for the Greek's 'come'; 'give our bread CONTINUALLY' (תמידית) — the Torah's תמיד of the continual bread of the Presence (Num 4:7), where Greek ἐπιούσιον is a hapax the Greek fathers could not parse; 'forgive our SINS' with Luke against Greek Matthew's 'debts'; 'do not bring us into the hands of testing' — word-for-word the Talmud's daily prayer (b. Ber. 60b); 'keep us from all evil' — Ps 121:7; no doxology. (2) 6:32 reads 'all these the BODIES (הגופים) seek' where Greek has 'the GENTILES (τὰ ἔθνη = הגוים)' — one Hebrew letter apart, and only the direction Hebrew-to-Greek explains the difference. (3) 6:30 'how much more US, of little faith (מקטני אמנה)' — the exact rabbinic idiom b. Sotah 48b ties to 'What shall I eat tomorrow?'; mss assimilate to 'you.' (4) 6:22-23 quote Prov 4:25 verbatim ('if your eyes look straight ahead') and end 'all your WAYS will be dark' (Prov 4:19); the base text states 'your body will NOT grow dark' where the Greek states the positive. (5) 6:21 ends 'where your treasure is — there,' without 'your heart will be' (all other mss add it). (6) 6:24 'you cannot serve El and the WORLD' — no mammon. (7) 6:28-29 'the rose of Sharon' (Song 2:1) against King Solomon (Song 1:1) — flower and king from the Song itself, glossed gilyon/lirio for Romance readers, as חנפים is glossed ipocrates (v. 2): the Hebrew words are native, the foreign words visitors. (8) 6:7 warns against 'the heretics (המינים),' not the Gentiles; 6:5 adds 'do not raise your voice' and quotes Hannah's warning against haughty speech (1 Sam 2:3). (9) 6:26 base text: 'your Father the Most High sustains YOU' (mss assimilate to 'them'). (10) 6:6 hides the one praying in Isa 26:20's own words ('shut your doors behind you'). Shem Tov's section divisions fall at vv. 2 (Perek 21), 5 (22), 16 (23), 19 (24), and 24 (25).
